paras: The Milltown, Georgia, committee beating of 1903 was a week of racial conflict in Milltown, Berrien County, in mid-May 1903, in which white residents hunted a Black railroad engineer, Seab Sharp, and a 'committee' beat an unnamed Black man. Sharp escaped, and white citizens petitioned the railroad's owner to stop employing Black engineers. The episode is known from a single Valdosta dispatch printed in the Savannah Morning News.

Sharp worked as an engineer on the Gress Railroad, on which Charlie Clanton, a white man, was conductor. At Naylor, Clanton ordered Sharp back to his engine to couple some flatcars; according to the dispatch, Sharp did not obey and the two quarreled. The correspondent wrote that Sharp then left his engine and gave the conductor 'a sound drubbing, being much the larger man.'

When the train returned to Milltown, Clanton's friends set out to find Sharp, but he 'dodged them and skipped out.' White citizens next drew up a petition asking Mr. Gress not to employ any more Black men as engineers on his trains. A Black man in Milltown who heard of the petition 'expressed himself pretty freely in regard to it,' and that night a committee called on him and gave him 'a thrashing.' The man is not named, and the dispatch does not say how badly he was hurt or who made up the committee.
No report of arrests, charges or any official response to the pursuit or the beating was found, and the coverage does not say whether Mr. Gress acted on the petition.

The Savannah Morning News ran the story on May 16, 1903, under the headline 'Whites and Negroes Row,' as the opening item of a column of Valdosta news notes. Its correspondent passed on 'reports from Milltown' and described the episode as 'trouble' between whites and Black residents that 'grew out of an assault made by' Sharp, a version that came from the white side. The beating was reported in two sentences without comment, followed in the same column by items on a proposed Black industrial college in Valdosta and a thunderstorm.
No other white paper and no Black paper in the coverage carried the story.

accounts.label: Valdosta correspondent (relaying reports from Milltown)
accounts.gist: Sharp refused Clanton's order, quarreled with him and beat him; Clanton's friends hunted Sharp, who escaped; whites petitioned against Black engineers, and a committee thrashed a Black man who criticized the petition.

framing.detail: The headline 'Whites and Negroes Row' presents the episode as mutual 'trouble' arising from Sharp's 'assault'; the committee beating is reported without comment between items on a Black industrial college and a thunderstorm.
